title: Book 4 — Melpomene, Chapter 192
paragraphs: In the land of the nomads, however, none of these creatures exists; but there are others, as follows: white-rump antelopes, gazelles, buffaloes, asses—not the horned kind but another sort that go without water (for in fact these never drink)—oryxes, whose horns are used to make the sides of the Phoenician lyre (this animal is about the size of an ox), small foxes, hyenas, porcupines, wild rams, wolves, jackals, panthers, boryes, land-crocodiles about three cubits long and very much like lizards, ostriches, and small snakes each with a single horn. These are the wild animals found in this country, besides those found elsewhere, except the stag and the wild boar; for Libya has no stags or wild boars at all. There are also in this country three kinds of mice: one called the “two-legged” mouse, another the zegeris (a Libyan word which in Greek means “hill”), and a third the “prickly” mouse. There are also weasels bred in the silphium, which are very like those of Tartessus. Such are the wild animals this land of the Libyans has, as far as we were able to learn by extending our inquiries as much as possible.
